scenarios.name: Aletsch Glacier
scenarios.title: A landscape in motion
scenarios.subtitle: Follow the flow of ice through the Swiss Alps.
scenarios.explanation: Actual optical observations show surface appearance. The supplied GOFF pair provides raw signed radar offsets and formal uncertainty; stable-ground bias correction and independent ice-motion validation remain necessary.

scenarios.name: Langtang Glacier
scenarios.title: Ice in the Himalayas
scenarios.subtitle: Explore a glacier in its mountain setting.
scenarios.explanation: Annual optical observations show surface changes. Import a matching GOFF science file to inspect signed radar-component rates with masks, correlation screening, formal uncertainty and acquisition-pair provenance.

scenarios.name: Columbia Glacier
scenarios.title: Ice on the coast
scenarios.subtitle: Explore a tidewater glacier surrounded by Alaska's mountains.
scenarios.explanation: Annual optical observations show surface changes. Quantitative tidewater-glacier motion requires a matching radar pair, quality screening, stable-ground bias assessment and independent validation.

scenarios.name: Sundarbans wetlands
scenarios.title: Water through the mangroves
scenarios.subtitle: Compare dry-season water signals in the Sundarbans.
scenarios.explanation: NDWI uses measured green and near-infrared reflectance. Tides, shadows and turbidity affect this water signal; it is not a confirmed flood or water-depth measurement.

scenarios.name: Rondônia forest
scenarios.title: A changing forest landscape
scenarios.subtitle: Inspect dry-season vegetation signals in Rondônia.
scenarios.explanation: NDVI uses measured red and near-infrared reflectance. Changes in greenness need land-cover and field evidence to establish forest loss, biomass or regrowth.
